document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2025–2026 22 026 Nederlands deel van een hogesnelheidsspoorverbinding Amsterdam-Brussel-Parijs en Utrecht-Arnhem-Duitse grens Nr. 528 BRIEF VAN DE STAATSSECRETARIS VAN INFRASTRUCTUUR EN WATERSTAAT Aan de Voorzitter van de Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal Den Haag, 27 augustus 2026 Op verzoek van de Kamer wordt u jaarlijks geïnformeerd over de ontwikkelingen op de Hogesnelheidslijn-Zuid (hierna: HSL)1. Over de HSL, gelegen tussen Hoofddorp en de Belgische grens, rijden zo’n 300 treinen per dag. Het is de enige hogesnelheidslijn in Nederland ontworpen om met 300 kilometer per uur over te rijden. Treinen kunnen echter momenteel over een deel van het traject maar tot 120 kilometer per uur rijden vanwege problemen met de infrastructuur. De lijn is opgeleverd in 2006 en sindsdien is Infraspeed verantwoordelijk voor het beheer en onderhoud van de HSL. Per 1 april 2031 neemt ProRail deze taken over. De HSL staat de komende jaren voor vier samenhangende opgaven die bepalend zijn voor een betrouwbare en toekomstbestendige hogesnel- heidsverbinding. De voorwaarden om dit beeld daadwerkelijk te realiseren zijn op cruciale onderdelen echter nog onvol doende geborgd. Dat vraagt om drie concrete vervolgstappen. 1. Verbind kritieke systeemkeuzes aan een toetsbare uitvoeringsagenda. Stel een aan het NPE gekoppelde uitvoeringsbijlage vast, met per kritieke schakel de verantwoordelijke partij, noodzakelijke besluiten, realisatieplanning, financieringsstatus, onderlinge afhankelijkheden en meetbare prestaties. Verbind de voortgangsrapportage aan de jaarlijkse klimaat- en begrotingscyclus. 2. In het Grevelingenmeer zijn er problemen met de waterkwaliteit en de ecologie, die voor een deel samenhangen met de fysische conditie van het watersysteem. De waargenomen problemen zijn o.a. het optreden van zuurstofloosheid in de diepe delen van de waterkolom, achteruitgang van het bodemleven en het voorkomen van matten van zwavelbacteriën zoals Beggiatoa op de bodem, in zowel de diepere delen als op relatief geringe waterdiepte. Zonder terugkeer van het getij, kan het Grevelingenmeer zich niet duurzaam herstellen en blijven de waterkwaliteit, natuurwaarden en ontwikkelmogelijkheden van het gebied onder grote druk staan. Door het aanleggen van een robuuste verbinding tussen de verschillende waterlichamen ontstaat dynamiek en nieuw leefgebied voor vis, schaal en schelpdieren, Natura 2000-soorten en habitattypen.

items.titel: Spatio-Temporal Dynamics of Urban Heat Islands and Sustainable Urban Development in a Rapidly Urbanizing Tropical City
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Rapid urbanization in tropical cities is intensifying surface urban heat island (SUHI) effects, posing significant challenges for sustainable urban planning. Hence, the present study investigates the spatio-temporal dynamics of land surface temperature (LST) and its relationship with vegetation and built-up indices in Raipur district, India, between 2015 and 2025. The multi-temporal Landsat imagery processed on the Google Earth Engine (GEE) was used to derive normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), normalized difference built-up index (NDBI), and LST, followed by SUHI intensity assessment and correlation analysis. The results reveal a clear spatial pattern in which urban and peri-urban areas exhibit elevated LST values, while vegetated rural zones act as thermal buffers. The NDVI-LST showed a consistent negative correlation (− 0.51 to − 0.33), highlighting the cooling role of vegetation, whereas LST-NDBI showed a consistent strong positive correlation (0.76–0.82), highlighting the warming impact of impervious surfaces. Change detection analysis indicates declining vegetation cover in peri-urban zones and expansion of built-up areas, contributing to outward propagation of thermal hotspots. Although SUHI intensity showed a relative decline over time, this was primarily driven by rising rural temperatures rather than urban cooling, suggesting regional thermal homogenization. items.titel: WILDLIFE UNDERPASSES AS INTEGRATED CIVIL AND ECOLOGICAL INFRASTRUCTURE: A Conceptual Design Framework for Highway Connectivity
items.samenvatting_bron: This report, titled “Wildlife Underpasses as Integrated Civil and Ecological Infrastructure: A Conceptual Design Framework for Highway Connectivity,” examines the integration of civil engineering principles and ecological considerations in the conceptual planning of wildlife underpasses along highways. The report discusses wildlife–vehicle collisions, habitat fragmentation, wildlife-crossing infrastructure, underpass planning and design considerations, drainage and hydraulic requirements, structural and geotechnical considerations, construction practices, maintenance, monitoring, and environmental management. It presents a conceptual framework intended to support safer wildlife movement and improved ecological connectivity across transportation infrastructure. The report is based on a review of relevant literature and published guidance. It is a conceptual technical study and does not claim original field surveys, site-specific investigations, or experimentally validated structural designs. Actual implementation would require site-specific ecological assessments, geotechnical investigations, hydraulic analysis, structural design, and approval by the relevant authorities. Institutional affiliation: Dr. D. Y. Patil Polytechnic, Kasaba Bawada, Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India.

It differs by its terete, sometimes 1–3 branched inflorescence (vs. sub-ancipitous more compressed beneath each floral bract, unbranching), burgundy-maroon flowers with a white and pink column (vs. vinaceous-red with dark purple column), incurved, arcuate, oblanceolate petals, 4.5–4.7 mm long (vs. elliptic, erect, 3 mm long), a lip with a sub-triangular mid-lobe (vs. oblong), and a column bearing setae which are hispid from near the middle to the apex (vs. apically stellate setae). items.titel: Evaluating environmental DNA metabarcoding for describing freshwater fish and shellfish occurrence in an Eastern Cascades watershed
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Objective Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding offers a promising, cost-effective tool to collect data across a large spatial scale, but analyzing these data poses several critical decisions that are uncommon to traditional field sampling. The objective of our study was to evaluate data collection, filtering, and analytical components of occurrence data generated using an eDNA metabarcoding approach. Methods During 2024, we collected replicated water samples from 89 sites distributed across the Wenatchee River Hydrologic Unit Code 8 watershed located in eastern Washington. We processed samples using two metabarcoding markers that targeted the cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 (CO1; Leray-XT) or 12S ribosomal RNA (MiFish-U) mitochondrial gene region, and we summarized differences in detection, taxonomic coverage, and data filtering requirements for each marker. Finalized metabarcoding data were used to fit occupancy models within a Bayesian framework. We evaluated model results with a focus on species-specific detection probability, the stability of predictions using the full data set and reduced numbers of visited sites, and comparisons between fitting models using a single-species or multispecies occupancy model approach. items.titel: An Open-Source Design Intervention Support Tool for Climate Resilience: Guiding Agroforestry in the Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems (WEFE) Nexus Systems
items.samenvatting_bron: The TRANS-SAHARA project supports climate change adaptation and mitigation in the Greater Northern African Region through scalable agroforestry systems embedded in a Water-Energy-Food-Ecosystems (WEFE) Nexus framework. This approach recognizes the interdependence of resources and promotes integrated, sustainable solutions in vulnerable contexts. The main objective of this research is to design and develop a decision-making support tool assisting researchers, policymakers, and local stakeholders in planning agroforestry interventions across regional Living Labs, local community-based sites where innovations are co-created and tested with project stakeholders. The tool aims to enable comprehensive analysis by integrating environmental, hydrological, socio-economic, and governance-related data, facilitating an inclusive evaluation of trade-offs and synergies. By incorporating multi-stakeholder perspectives, it supports more holistic and robust decision-making—an essential feature given the inherently multi-factor nature of the optimization problem the project aims to address. Effective collaboration and impact in sustainability research hinge on the open sharing of data and metadata. The tool is built upon Eurac’s research data infrastructure, known as the Environmental Data Platform (EDP). Intratracheal microspray delivery of iohexol for sustained lung-parenchymal enhancement in preclinical micro-computed tomography: A feasibility and acute-safety study in mice
items.samenvatting_bron: by Sheng-Chieh Lin, Kuo-Kai Lin, Kevin Aristyo, Hong-Min Lin, Wei-Hung Liu, Erh-Hsuan Hsieh, Ching-Li Tseng Preclinical thoracic micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is constrained by the brief pulmonary enhancement window of intravenously (IV) administered iodinated contrast, which the kidneys clear rapidly. We performed a feasibility study in mice comparing IV tail-vein injection with intratracheal microspray instillation of the clinical agent iohexol. Mice received iohexol (100 µL, 500 mg/mL) by either route. Whole-body projections were acquired to 120 min and thoracic sections to 30 min, each animal scanned before contrast in the same session. Contrast distribution was recorded by compartment and quantified from regions of interest. IV delivery produced vascular and cardiac opacification with progressive bladder accumulation, which was the largest signal in every IV animal by 120 min. Intratracheal delivery produced widespread, comparatively uniform lung-parenchymal opacification at 5, 15 and 30 min with no discrete bladder opacity at any time; coronal thoracic signal was 0.77 at 5 min and 0.72 at 30 min, against 0.09 to 0.19 after IV injection. Acute safety was assessed at 5 and 29 h by serum biochemistry and histopathology against untreated controls. ALT, AST and blood urea nitrogen did not differ among groups.
